title: X-rays, CT and MRI scans
examples: What is the difference between an X-ray and an MRI?
Are all medical scans safe to use?
How do these machines actually see inside us?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how doctors see inside the body. We will look at three main tools. These tools are X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs. They help doctors see bones and soft tissues.

X-rays use a small beam of energy to pass through the body. Different materials block this beam differently. Bones are very dense, so they block many X-rays. This makes them appear white on the picture.
A CT scan takes many X-ray pictures from different angles. It then puts these pictures together like slices of bread. This gives a much more detailed view than a single X-ray picture.
MRI scans do not use X-rays at all. Instead, they use very strong magnets and radio waves. These magnets make the water molecules in your body line up. The machine then detects how they realign.

draw.text: MRI: Strong magnets and radio waves

explain.say: When doctors use these scans, they are looking for problems. They want to see if bones are broken or if soft tissues are inflamed. It is a way to see inside without cutting you open.

Imagine a baker needing to check if a loaf of bread has a weak spot. The X-ray shows the hard crust (bones) clearly. The CT scan shows the internal structure in detailed slices. The MRI is like checking the moisture level everywhere inside.

faq.q: Are X-rays dangerous to my body?
faq.a: X-rays use a small amount of energy to create pictures. They are safe when used correctly by trained medical professionals. You might also hear people ask if they hurt, or if they are bad for me.
asks: Is it okay to get many X-rays?

faq.q: What is the main difference between CT and MRI?
faq.a: The main difference is that CT uses X-rays to take many slices. MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to look at soft parts. Some people ask if they are related, or which one is better for knees.
asks: Do I need both a CT and an MRI?
Which scan is better for ligaments?

faq.q: Do I need to prepare for an MRI scan?
faq.a: Yes, you usually need to remove metal objects before an MRI. This is because the machine uses very strong magnets. You might also ask if I can bring my phone, or if I need to take off my jewelry.
asks: Can I wear metal clothes for an MRI?
What should I bring to an MRI appointment?

faq.q: Why do bones show up so clearly on X-rays?
faq.a: Bones are made of hard minerals, which are very dense materials. These dense materials absorb many of the X-rays. The machine detects this blockage, making the bones appear bright white on the film. You might wonder why soft tissues look different, or what makes bone so hard.
asks: Why are bones white on the picture?
What makes bone block X-rays so well?

faq.a: Most of the time, the scans are painless, though you might hear some loud knocking noises. For an MRI, you might need to lie very still inside the machine. You could ask if I need to hold my breath, or if it is scary.
asks: Will I feel pain during the scan?
Do I have to stay still the whole time?

facts: CT scans create cross-sectional images of the body.
MRI scans use magnetic fields and radio waves.
Bones appear white because they are dense and absorb X-rays.

quiz.say: Which scan uses powerful magnets and radio waves?
quiz.why: MRI uses magnetic fields to detect water molecules in the body.

wrong.1: X-rays use beams of energy, not magnets.
wrong.2: CT scans use X-rays taken from many angles.
wrong.3: Ultrasound uses sound waves, not magnets.

quiz.say: If a body part is very dense, how does it show up on an X-ray?
quiz.why: Dense materials, like bone, block X-rays, making them appear white.

wrong.1: Black means the X-rays passed through easily.
wrong.2: Grey means the material is partially blocking the beam.
wrong.3: It will show up, but it will be very bright.

quiz.say: What does the process of taking many X-ray angles and stacking them create?
quiz.why: Stitching many angles together creates detailed slices, which is the CT scan.

wrong.1: A simple X-ray is just one picture, not many slices.
wrong.2: MRI uses magnets, not multiple X-ray angles.
wrong.3: This is a drawing, not a machine scan.
